name: gizza-ai/nmea-to-csv
summary: Convert a raw NMEA 0183 GPS log into a clean CSV track table.

tool.description: Convert a raw NMEA 0183 GPS/GNSS serial log into a CSV track table, one row per positional fix. Sentences of the same cycle (shared UTC time) are merged: GGA supplies altitude / fix quality / satellite count / HDOP, RMC supplies date / speed / course, GLL is a position fallback, VTG fills speed + course, ZDA supplies the date, GSA backfills HDOP. Columns: timestamp (added when a date is known), time, latitude, longitude, altitude_<unit>, fix, satellites, hdop, speed_<unit>, course. coordinates picks decimal-degrees or DMS; altitude_unit is m/ft; speed_unit is knots/kmh/mph; delimiter picks the separator; header toggles the header row; validate_checksum drops lines that fail their *XX checksum. Paste the log in the 'nmea' field. Runs entirely in-browser; nothing is uploaded.

altitude_unit.description: Unit for the altitude column. m (default) keeps GGA metres; ft converts to feet. The column header is altitude_m or altitude_ft accordingly.

coordinates.description: Coordinate output format. decimal (default) writes signed decimal degrees (e.g. 48.1173, -11.5167); dms writes degrees-minutes-seconds with a hemisphere letter (e.g. 48°07'02.28"N).

delimiter.description: Output CSV field separator. Default comma. Use semicolon for comma-decimal locales, tab for TSV, or pipe.

header.description: Emit the column-name header row. Default true; set false for a headerless CSV.

nmea.description: The NMEA 0183 log to convert. Paste the raw serial text — one sentence per line such as $GPGGA,... , $GNRMC,... , $GPGLL,... , $GPVTG,... , $GPZDA,... , $GPGSA,... (any talker prefix: GP/GN/GL/GA/GB).

speed_unit.description: Unit for the speed column. knots (default) matches NMEA's native speed-over-ground; kmh is km/h; mph is miles/h. The column header is speed_knots, speed_kmh, or speed_mph.

validate_checksum.description: Verify each line's NMEA *XX checksum and drop any sentence that fails it. Default false (parse every line). Lines that carry no checksum are always parsed.
